text: Madhur Canteen (Bengali: মধুর রেস্তোরা, romanized: Modhur restora, lit. 'Madhu's canteen') is a well-known landmark in the history of Dhaka University and in Bangladesh's national politics due to its association with various political movements that originated from the university. The canteen's current location holds significant architectural and heritage value. Madhusudan Dey (Modhu), the canteen's founder, is a key figure in the region's socio-political history; he was killed on 25 March 1971 during Operation Searchlight when the Pakistan Army attacked Dhaka University, taking him to Jagannath Hall where he was executed along with many university students. Madhusudan Dey was injured, arrested, and killed in the early morning hours of 26 March 1971 after the military stormed his house, during which his wife, son, and daughter-in-law were also killed. After the Liberation War, Arun Kumar Dey took over the management of the canteen. The canteen was established in 1921 when Madhusudan Dey, aged 15, came to Dhaka with his father, Aditya Chandra, who, with university authorities' permission, began selling food on the campus, which at the time was located in the present Dhaka Medical College building. The canteen was later relocated when the Arts Faculty moved to a new building at Nilkhet. Madhur Canteen played a central role in the Bangladesh Liberation Movement and was a focal point for political activism, including the Language Movements of 1948 and 1952, the 1949 movement by fourth-class Dhaka University employees, student protests against the university's black laws (kala kanoon), and the 1969 mass uprising in East Pakistan. During these events, it served as a social epicentre for student leaders and activists. The Pakistani army targeted the canteen on 25 March 1971, marking the beginning of Operation Searchlight. The canteen suffered severe damage during the liberation war and was subsequently reconstructed. It was relocated to an old structure that previously served as the Durbar Hall of the Dhaka Nawabs, a building constructed starting in 1873 and continued over several years. In 1906, a conference held in this building, sponsored by Nawab Bahadur Sir Khwaja Salimullah, the Nawab of Dhaka, led to the formation of the All-India Muslim League. The canteen continues to be a significant community gathering place. In 1995, a statue of Madhusudan Dey, created by Toufiq Hosen Khan, a student of fine arts, was installed in front of the canteen.
